# etcdserver: lease ids generated by two members collide when their member ids agree in the low 15 bits

A lease granted without an explicit id gets `reqIDGen.Next() & (1<<63 - 1)`
([`v3_server.go:438`](https://github.com/upamanyus/etcd/blob/249d76bea78d0c8980251d5fa7b26c35ef21263a/server/etcdserver/v3_server.go#L438)).
The generator puts the member id's low 16 bits in bits 48–63
([`idutil/id.go:57`](https://github.com/upamanyus/etcd/blob/249d76bea78d0c8980251d5fa7b26c35ef21263a/pkg/idutil/id.go#L57)),
and the mask clears bit 63, the prefix's top bit. So two members whose ids agree in the low 15 bits
(rather than 16, as for request ids: `etcd-request-id-member-prefix.md`) generate the same lease ids.
The second grant of a colliding id gets `ErrLeaseExists`. If the first lease was revoked, the
second grant silently re-uses its id.

**Why not an issue:** no test; found by code reading (the scope of the multi-member lease example,
2026-11-06). The outcome is an error the client can retry (`ErrLeaseExists`), or a fresh lease
under a previously used id, which etcd does not promise against. Member ids colliding in 15 bits
are as unlikely as for request ids.

## Proof

no: in the revocable mode the proof boots a single member (`srvMemberBoot_alloc`'s `hpfx`,
`kvGrantIds`' one prefix, `Proof/go_etcd_io/etcd/server/v3/etcdserver/InvRequest.lean`), and in the
monotone mode an id collision is the `ErrLeaseExists` the specs allow. A multi-member revocable
cluster (the lease plan's step 2) would need a premise that the members' ids differ in the low
15 bits, or a per-prefix ever-set.
